home.title: From run sheet to cue list in grandMA3
home.lead: Upload the run sheet you got from production – PDF, Word or Excel. In a minute you have a macro that builds the cue list on the console: one named cue per item, in the right order.
home.disclaimer: Not affiliated with MA Lighting. grandMA3 is a trademark of MA Lighting Technology GmbH.
home.stepsTitle: Three cues, and the sequence is built

upload.title: Upload the run sheet
upload.text: Drop in the file from production, or paste the text. Columns like #, Start and Title are found automatically.

review.title: Check the cues
review.text: One row per cue, in the right order. Edit names, split a set list into sub-cues and fix anything that was read wrong.

console.title: Import on the console
console.text: Download a macro, import it on grandMA3 and run it once. Your sequence is built with named, empty cues.

home.ctaSub: Free to try. No account needed.

formats.title: Reads the run sheet as it arrives
formats.text: Messy tables, merged cells and several sheets are fine. No reformatting, no copying into a template.

private.title: Your files never leave your computer
private.text: Everything is read in your browser. Nothing is uploaded, so you can use it with confidential shows.

numbers.title: Cue numbers follow the run sheet
numbers.text: Item 12 becomes cue 12 on the console. A set list splits into sub-cues (12.1, 12.2) in one click, and items without a number fit in between their neighbours.

story: CueSetter started backstage. Before every show the run sheet arrived as a PDF, often late. We work in the industry and have seen it again and again.
Now it takes a minute, and the time goes to the lighting.
home.tagline: Run sheet in. Cue list out.
home.finalLead: Try it with your next run sheet, or see how it works with our sample.
home.storyKicker: Made by the industry, for the industry
home.storyQuote: Every item had to be typed into the console by hand, while the lighting waited.

faq.a: PDF with text, Word (.docx) and Excel (.xlsx), straight from production. You can also paste text. Scanned PDFs (images) and old .doc and .xls files can’t be read; save them as .docx or .xlsx, or paste the text.

faq.q: What if my run sheet is called something else?
faq.a: It works the same whatever the document is called: run sheet, running order, run of show, rundown, show flow, cue sheet or programme. What matters is a list of items with times or numbers, in PDF, Word, Excel or as text.

faq.q: Is my run sheet uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Everything is read in the browser on your own computer. The run sheet is never sent to us or any other server, so you can use it for confidential productions.

faq.q: How do I get the cue list into grandMA3?
faq.a: Download the macro as a ZIP and unzip it to the root of a USB stick. On the console, open Show Creator, choose Macros and the USB stick, import the macro and run it once. It builds the sequence with one named cue per item. If the import fails, you can paste the commands into the command line instead.

faq.q: Which grandMA3 versions does it work with?
faq.a: The macro is tested on most recent versions of grandMA3, and should in theory work on every version of grandMA3. If it doesn’t work on your version, we’d like to hear from you at hello@cuesetter.com.

faq.q: What happens to the cue numbers?
faq.a: Cue numbers follow the # in the run sheet. A set list can be split into sub-cues (12.1, 12.2) in one click, and items without a number get a number between their neighbours, for example 12.5. You can also choose running numbers 1, 2, 3.
It’s free to try, no account needed.

excel.metaTitle: Excel run sheet to grandMA3 cue list – CueSetter
excel.metaDescription: Turn an Excel run sheet (.xlsx) into a named grandMA3 cue list. CueSetter finds the header row and columns, reads every sheet and makes a macro that builds the sequence. Runs in your browser.
excel.title: Excel run sheet to grandMA3 cue list
excel.lead: Upload the .xlsx file from production as it is. CueSetter finds the header row and the columns for number, time and title, and gives you a grandMA3 macro that builds one named cue per row.
excel.readsTitle: What CueSetter reads in an Excel run sheet

reads.title: Every sheet in the workbook
reads.text: One sheet per day or stage is fine. Pick the sheet you need; hidden sheets are skipped. The title above the table, or else the sheet name, becomes the sequence name.

reads.title: The header row, wherever it is
reads.text: Title and info rows at the top are skipped. The header row can be anywhere in the first 20 rows, with headers like #, Start, Time, Duration, Title or Item.

reads.title: Times as Excel shows them
reads.text: Cells formatted as time come out as 18:30, not 0.77. Repeated header rows further down are skipped.

reads.title: Items over several rows
reads.text: A row without a number or time continues the item above, so a long item or a set list stays one cue, ready to split into sub-cues.

steps.title: Upload the .xlsx file
steps.text: Drop the file into CueSetter. If the workbook has several sheets with a run sheet, choose the one for the show.

steps.title: Check the columns and cues
steps.text: The columns found are marked. Pick another if one is wrong, then edit names and split a set list into sub-cues.

steps.title: Import on grandMA3
steps.text: Unzip the macro to the root of a USB stick. In Show Creator, choose Macros and the stick, import it and run it once. The sequence is built with one named cue per item.

faq.q: How do I get an Excel cue list into grandMA3?
faq.a: grandMA3 imports macros as XML files. CueSetter turns the spreadsheet into a grandMA3 macro: import it from a USB stick and run it once, and the sequence is built with one named cue per item.

faq.q: Can I use .xls or CSV files?
faq.a: Old .xls files can’t be read; open them in Excel and save as .xlsx. A CSV file can be opened in Excel and saved as .xlsx too, or you can copy the rows with the header and paste them into CueSetter as text.

faq.q: Is the file uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. The file is read in your browser on your own computer and is never sent to us or any other server.

pdf.metaTitle: PDF run sheet to grandMA3 cue list – CueSetter
pdf.metaDescription: Turn a PDF run sheet into a named grandMA3 cue list. CueSetter reads the table in the PDF, finds the columns and makes a macro that builds the sequence. Runs in your browser.
pdf.title: PDF run sheet to grandMA3 cue list
pdf.lead: Most run sheets arrive as a PDF. Upload it as it is: CueSetter reads the table, finds the columns for number, time and title, and gives you a grandMA3 macro that builds one named cue per item.
pdf.readsTitle: What CueSetter reads in a PDF run sheet

reads.title: The table, from where the text sits
reads.text: Columns are found from the header row and where the text sits on the page. No need to copy anything into a spreadsheet first.

reads.title: Several pages
reads.text: Items continue across page breaks. A header row repeated on every page, and the page headers above it, are skipped.

reads.title: From any program
reads.text: Exported from Word, Excel, Google Docs or a rundown tool: any PDF with text can be read. The title at the top becomes the sequence name.

reads.title: Scanned PDFs
reads.text: A scan is an image with no text to read. Copy the text out of it (or run it through OCR) and paste it into CueSetter instead.

steps.title: Upload the PDF
steps.text: Drop the file into CueSetter, or open it from your phone or computer. It is read in your browser.

steps.title: Check the columns and cues
steps.text: The columns found are marked. Pick another if one is wrong, then edit names and split a set list into sub-cues.

steps.title: Import on grandMA3
steps.text: Unzip the macro to the root of a USB stick. In Show Creator, choose Macros and the stick, import it and run it once. The sequence is built with one named cue per item.

faq.q: How do I get a PDF run sheet into grandMA3?
faq.a: grandMA3 imports macros as XML files, not PDFs. CueSetter reads the PDF and makes a grandMA3 macro: import it from a USB stick and run it once, and the sequence is built with one named cue per item.

faq.q: Why does it say there is no text in my PDF?
faq.a: The PDF is most likely scanned, which makes every page an image. Ask production for the original file (Word, Excel or an exported PDF), or copy the text out and paste it into CueSetter.

faq.q: Is the file uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. The file is read in your browser on your own computer and is never sent to us or any other server.

word.metaTitle: Word run sheet to grandMA3 cue list – CueSetter
word.metaDescription: Turn a Word run sheet (.docx) into a named grandMA3 cue list. CueSetter reads the tables in the document, finds the columns and makes a macro that builds the sequence. Runs in your browser.
word.title: Word run sheet to grandMA3 cue list
word.lead: Upload the .docx file from production as it is. CueSetter reads the table, finds the columns for number, time and title, and gives you a grandMA3 macro that builds one named cue per item.
word.readsTitle: What CueSetter reads in a Word run sheet

reads.title: Tables, merged cells too
reads.text: Columns are found from the header row. Merged cells and several lines in one cell are fine.

reads.title: Several tables
reads.text: If the document has more than one table, for example one per day, choose the one for the show.

reads.title: No table at all
reads.text: A run sheet written as lines, like “18:30 Doors open”, is read line by line, the same way as pasted text.

reads.title: The title becomes the sequence name
reads.text: The first line above the table, usually the name of the show, is used as the sequence name. You can change it before export.

steps.title: Upload the .docx file
steps.text: Drop the file into CueSetter. If the document has several tables, choose the one for the show.

steps.title: Check the columns and cues
steps.text: The columns found are marked. Pick another if one is wrong, then edit names and split a set list into sub-cues.

steps.title: Import on grandMA3
steps.text: Unzip the macro to the root of a USB stick. In Show Creator, choose Macros and the stick, import it and run it once. The sequence is built with one named cue per item.

faq.q: How do I get a Word run sheet into grandMA3?
faq.a: grandMA3 imports macros as XML files. CueSetter reads the Word document and makes a grandMA3 macro: import it from a USB stick and run it once, and the sequence is built with one named cue per item.
Old .doc files can’t be read. Open the file in Word and save it as .docx, or export it as PDF, and try again.

faq.q: Is the file uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. The file is read in your browser on your own computer and is never sent to us or any other server.
